title: Lock down device management
blurb: SSH only, local admin accounts, a management ACL and login protection on a router.
scenario: R1 is a new edge router. Today anyone can reach it with Telnet, and it still has no local accounts. Lock down management so that only the network team, from the management subnet **10.10.99.0/24**, can log in, and only over **SSH version 2**.
topology:
Mgmt PC 10.10.99.25 ── [10.10.99.0/24] ── R1 ── Internet
                                     domain: scor.lab
objectives: Generate RSA keys and turn on SSH version 2
Create a privilege 15 local admin and an enable secret
Allow logins only from the management subnet
Restrict the VTY lines to SSH with local login and an idle timeout
Slow down password guessing and turn off the HTTP server

steps.title: Turn on SSH version 2
steps.learn: SSH needs an RSA key pair, and IOS names the key after the **hostname** and **domain name**, so the domain must be set first. Keys of 2048 bits or more are the current minimum, and **SSH version 2** fixes the weaknesses of version 1.
steps.task: Enter global configuration mode. Set the domain name to **scor.lab**, generate a **2048**-bit RSA key, and set SSH to **version 2**.
steps.hint: Start with `configure terminal`. The commands are `ip domain name`, `crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048` and `ip ssh version 2`.

commands.note: The domain name is set. Older IOS versions spell it `ip domain-name`.

alt: crypto key generate rsa general-keys modulus 2048
commands.output:
The name for the keys will be: R1.scor.lab
% The key modulus size is 2048 bits
% Generating 2048 bit RSA keys, keys will be non-exportable...
[OK] (elapsed time was 2 seconds)
%SSH-5-ENABLED: SSH 1.99 has been enabled
commands.note: The key pair R1.scor.lab exists, and SSH turned on automatically as 1.99, which allows both versions.
Only SSH version 2 is accepted now.

steps.why: SSH 1.99 means "versions 1 and 2". Setting version 2 explicitly refuses the older, weaker protocol.

steps.title: Create the admin account
steps.learn: Use `secret` instead of `password`. A `secret` is stored as a strong hash (type 9 scrypt or type 8 PBKDF2 with `algorithm-type`; type 5 MD5 by default on older code). A `password` is plain text, or reversible type 7 with `service password-encryption`.
steps.task: Create a local user **admin** at **privilege 15** with the secret **Sc0rLab!**, and set the enable secret to **En4bleLab!**.
steps.hint: `username admin privilege 15 secret Sc0rLab!` and `enable secret En4bleLab!`

alt: username admin privilege 15 algorithm-type scrypt secret Sc0rLab!
username admin privilege 15 algorithm-type sha256 secret Sc0rLab!
commands.note: The admin user lands directly in privileged EXEC mode at login.
The enable secret is stored hashed.

steps.title: Build the management ACL
steps.learn: A **standard ACL** matches only the source address, which is all you need to decide who may open a session to the router.
steps.task: Create a named standard ACL called **MGMT** that permits **10.10.99.0/24**.
steps.hint: `ip access-list standard MGMT`, then `permit 10.10.99.0 0.0.0.255`. ACLs use a wildcard mask, not a subnet mask.

commands.note: Every ACL ends with an implicit deny, so other sources are refused.

steps.title: Restrict the VTY lines
steps.learn: The VTY lines are the virtual terminals that SSH and Telnet sessions land on. `access-class` applies an ACL to sessions arriving on the lines, `transport input` picks the protocols that are allowed, and `login local` checks the local user database.
steps.task: Configure **line vty 0 4**: allow only **SSH**, authenticate against the **local** database, apply ACL **MGMT** inbound, and disconnect idle sessions after **10 minutes**.
steps.hint: Enter `line vty 0 4`, then `transport input ssh`, `login local`, `access-class MGMT in` and `exec-timeout 10 0`.

commands.note: Telnet is now refused on these lines.
Logins are checked against the local usernames.
Idle sessions close after 10 minutes and 0 seconds.

steps.title: Slow down password guessing
steps.learn: `login block-for` makes the router refuse all logins for a while after too many failures in a short window (quiet mode). The built-in **HTTP server** is a management interface you aren't using, so turn it off to shrink the attack surface.
steps.task: Block logins for **120 seconds** after **3** failed attempts within **60 seconds**, and turn off the **HTTP server**.
steps.hint: `login block-for 120 attempts 3 within 60` and `no ip http server`. Both are global commands, so they work even from the line prompt.

commands.note: Three failures in 60 seconds now trigger 120 seconds of quiet mode.
The plain HTTP server is off.

steps.title: Check your work
steps.learn: Think through how the pieces combine before testing them from a real client.
steps.task: Answer the question about the finished configuration.
steps.question: A technician at **10.10.50.20** opens SSH to R1 with the correct admin password. What happens?
steps.hint: Which of the line settings looks at the source address?

options.text: The session is refused because the source isn't permitted by ACL MGMT.
The login works, because the username and password are correct.
options.why: `access-class MGMT in` is checked before the login prompt. 10.10.50.20 isn't in 10.10.99.0/24.

options.text: The router falls back to Telnet for that address.
options.why: `transport input ssh` allows only SSH, and there's no fallback to another protocol.

options.text: R1 enters quiet mode for 120 seconds.
options.why: Quiet mode follows failed logins. This session never reaches a login prompt.

steps.title: Verify SSH
steps.learn: Verification commands run in privileged EXEC mode. From configuration mode, put **do** in front of them, or type `end` first.
steps.task: Display the SSH status to confirm that version 2 is running.
steps.hint: `do show ip ssh` from configuration mode, or `end` and then `show ip ssh`.

commands.output:
SSH Enabled - version 2.0
Authentication methods:publickey,keyboard-interactive,password
Authentication timeout: 120 secs; Authentication retries: 3
Minimum expected Diffie Hellman key size : 2048 bits
IOS Keys in SECSH format(ssh-rsa, base64 encoded): R1.scor.lab
commands.note: SSH version 2.0 is enabled with the R1.scor.lab key.

summary: SSH version 2 with a 2048-bit RSA key, a privilege 15 local admin with a hashed secret, VTY lines limited to SSH from 10.10.99.0/24 with local login and a 10-minute timeout, login quiet mode after repeated failures, and the HTTP server turned off.
